originality.rationale: The claim is a density-conditioned classification of finite strong prefix-closed chain relations, an exact Stirling-rank and serial distribution, and a count of the fibres over all induced nuclei. The 2022 primary source defines the class but neither counts it nor provides the density partition test. A highly relevant published 2026 result supplies the entire ambient (n+1)! column-cutoff normal form, which is credited and NOT claimed new; another published result has a Bell-number-difference census for a different relation class, not the present theorem. Complete inspected texts and independent searches found no statement-level implication covering the new density test plus semantic fibres. Risk remains from an inaccessible original 1981 article and unindexed equivalent combinatorial formulations.
residual_risks: Goldblatt 1981 original full article inaccessible, so a historical formulation of the density-partition theorem cannot be excluded.

Unindexed order-theoretic partition or fixed-point formulations may duplicate aspects of the result; database retrieval does not prove uniqueness.
The standard number of finite-chain nuclei and classical Bell/Stirling sequences are not itself novel; significance rests on the exact semantic classification and fibres.

value.rationale: Strong dense Goldblatt-style frames form an established semantic family relevant to propositional lax logic. On the natural entire infinite family of finite linearly ordered carriers, the result does more than enumerate a known Bell sequence: it classifies the density boundary inside a known factorial ambient frame family, resolves the full reflexive-world and serial distributions, and identifies the precise semantic quotient of raw relations into nuclei with exact per-nucleus fibre cardinalities. The relation-to-operator multiplicity is a naturally motivated structural invariant, useful when avoiding redundant relational presentations in finite semantics. It is not an arbitrary tiny fixed-size or renamed textbook exercise; ordinary Bell/Stirling counting and the ambient cutoff normal form are credited.
